button-game.title: Button Game
button-game.preview: A one-minute reaction game with moving targets and physical-looking scores.
button-game.credit: Creative direction and authorship: Babuni.dev. AI-assisted implementation and editorial summaries are identified in the source record.
button-game.body: The game begins with the first press of a moving turquoise button and a 60-second clock. Presses release visible numbers into a bounded playfield; collecting and combining them becomes part of the game. Creative direction and authorship belong to Babuni.dev.

button-game.title: Play and combinations
button-game.preview: Quick Strikes, bouncing numbers, score collection and time rewards.
button-game.credit: Creative direction and authorship: Babuni.dev. AI-assisted implementation and editorial summaries are identified in the source record.
button-game.body: Quick Strike rewards the first hit just after a target appears. Floating values collide and merge before their earned score reaches the collector. Special combinations include 21 → 42 and 37 → 73. Selected milestones award visible time bonuses. These details are documented in the game concept; this portfolio is not a separate gameplay verification.

button-game.title: Play together on Wi-Fi
button-game.preview: One Android phone hosts the browser game and shared high scores.
button-game.credit: Creative direction and authorship: Babuni.dev. AI-assisted implementation and editorial summaries are identified in the source record.
button-game.body: Serve on Wi-Fi lets the Android app host the game for nearby players joining through an address or QR code. The Android host owns the shared leaderboard. This is parallel local play with shared rankings, rather than synchronized game physics between players.

button-game.title: Development story
button-game.preview: From an older Flash game to browser play, score physics and Android hosting.
button-game.credit: Creative direction and authorship: Babuni.dev. AI-assisted implementation and editorial summaries are identified in the source record.
button-game.body: The repository preserves the original Flash artifact, an earlier reconstruction and the evolving browser/Android game. Its journal records Babuni.dev’s directions and corrections alongside AI implementation. Visible score transfers, special-number choreography and host-owned persistence evolved through those iterations.
